Track how [latex]\text{length}\bmod3[/latex] evolves across recursive calls, since only the [latex]\text{length}\%3==1[/latex] branch ever adds [latex]1[/latex] to the final result (the other two branches just recurse without contributing anything):

- If current length [latex]\equiv0\ (\text{mod }3)[/latex]: recurse with length reduced by [latex]1[/latex] (no addition) → new length [latex]\equiv2\ (\text{mod }3)[/latex].
- If current length [latex]\equiv1\ (\text{mod }3)[/latex]: add [latex]1[/latex], recurse with length reduced by [latex]1[/latex] → new length [latex]\equiv0\ (\text{mod }3)[/latex].
- If current length [latex]\equiv2\ (\text{mod }3)[/latex]: recurse with length reduced by [latex]2[/latex] (no addition) → new length [latex]\equiv0\ (\text{mod }3)[/latex].

Once the length's residue enters the cycle [latex]0\to2\to0\to2\to\cdots[/latex], it can never return to residue [latex]1[/latex] again (the only transitions available from [latex]0[/latex] and [latex]2[/latex] both lead back into this same two-value cycle). So the "[latex]+1[/latex]" branch can only ever be triggered once in any call chain — specifically only if the very first (initial) call's length happens to be [latex]\equiv1\ (\text{mod }3)[/latex]. After that single possible addition, the recursion is permanently locked into the non-adding [latex]0/2[/latex] cycle until it terminates at the base case.

So the maximum possible total returned value, over all valid inputs, is just [latex]1[/latex].

Answer: 1

Trace the program step by step:

[latex]a=5,\ b=11,\ c=20[/latex].
[latex]\text{ptr}=\&a[/latex] (ptr now points to [latex]a[/latex]).
[latex]{*}\text{ptr}=c[/latex] → sets [latex]a=20[/latex] (since ptr points to [latex]a[/latex], and we assign it [latex]c[/latex]'s current value [latex]20[/latex]).
[latex]\text{ptr}=\&c[/latex] (ptr now points to [latex]c[/latex] instead).
[latex]a={*}(\&b)[/latex] → sets [latex]a=b=11[/latex] (overwriting the earlier [latex]20[/latex]).
[latex]c={*}\text{ptr}-a[/latex] → [latex]{*}\text{ptr}[/latex] is [latex]c[/latex] itself (since ptr points to [latex]c[/latex]), whose value is still [latex]20[/latex] (unchanged since it was first set); so [latex]c=20-a=20-11=9[/latex].

[latex]\text{printf}[/latex] prints the final value of [latex]c[/latex], which is [latex]9[/latex].

Answer: 9

First, note [latex]\text{bar}(n)[/latex] repeatedly integer-halves [latex]n[/latex] until reaching [latex]1[/latex], counting the number of halvings — this is exactly [latex]\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor[/latex].

[latex]\text{foo}(n)=1+\text{foo}(\text{bar}(n))[/latex] for [latex]n>1[/latex], and [latex]\text{foo}(1)=1[/latex]. So [latex]\text{foo}(n)[/latex] counts [latex]1[/latex] plus the number of times we must apply [latex]\text{bar}[/latex] (i.e. take [latex]\lfloor\log_2\cdot\rfloor[/latex]) starting from [latex]n[/latex] to eventually reach [latex]1[/latex].

Build up the smallest [latex]n[/latex] achieving each target value of [latex]\text{foo}[/latex]:
- [latex]\text{foo}(n)=1[/latex]: smallest [latex]n=1[/latex].
- [latex]\text{foo}(n)=2[/latex]: need [latex]\text{bar}(n)=1[/latex], i.e. [latex]\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor=1[/latex]: smallest [latex]n=2[/latex].
- [latex]\text{foo}(n)=3[/latex]: need [latex]\text{bar}(n)=2[/latex]: smallest [latex]n=2^2=4[/latex].
- [latex]\text{foo}(n)=4[/latex]: need [latex]\text{bar}(n)=4[/latex]: smallest [latex]n=2^4=16[/latex].
- [latex]\text{foo}(n)=5[/latex]: need [latex]\text{bar}(n)=16[/latex]: smallest [latex]n=2^{16}=65536[/latex].

Answer: 65536

Trace the call [latex]\text{func(9, 10)}[/latex] (parameters [latex]i=9,\,j=10[/latex] inside func, independent copies of main's variables):

1. Condition [latex]i\lt j[/latex] i.e. [latex]9\lt 10[/latex] is true, so we enter the block.
2. Inside the block, a new, block-scoped variable [latex]\text{int } i=0[/latex] is declared — this shadows/hides the outer parameter [latex]i[/latex] only within this inner block.
3. The while loop runs while this inner [latex]i\lt 10[/latex]: it executes [latex]10[/latex] times, each time doing [latex]j{+}{=}2[/latex] (affecting the outer/parameter [latex]j[/latex]) and incrementing the inner [latex]i[/latex] (from [latex]0[/latex] up to [latex]10[/latex], at which point the loop stops).
4. Once the block ends, the inner [latex]i[/latex] goes out of scope entirely; the outer parameter [latex]i[/latex] (value [latex]9[/latex]) was never touched by anything in the block.
5. [latex]\text{printf("\%d", i)}[/latex] refers to the (unshadowed, outer) parameter [latex]i[/latex], which is still [latex]9[/latex].

Answer: 9
